name: Muslin-Shroud
geological_features: Fine dust coating creating uniform surface texture
specific_features: Thin dust layer giving the planet a muslin-draped appearance
Perfectly preserved ancient probe wreckage from unknown origin
description: Muslin-Shroud is a small barren world covered in a uniform layer of extremely fine dust that gives the entire surface a soft, draped appearance, as though the planet has been covered in muslin cloth. The dust is so fine that it behaves almost like a liquid under the weak gravity, flowing slowly into depressions and coating every surface with an even layer that erases topographic detail. Impact craters that should be visible from orbit are hidden beneath the dust mantle, their presence detectable only through gravity mapping and ground-penetrating radar.

The thin atmosphere is dusty and dry, carrying particles that reduce visibility and coat equipment within hours of deployment. The dust infiltrates everything—seals, joints, optical instruments, breathing filters—with a persistence that makes extended surface operations a maintenance nightmare. The landscape is monochromatic, a uniform gray-tan in every direction, with no landmarks visible above the dust layer. Navigation requires constant instrument reference, as visual orientation is nearly impossible in the featureless terrain.

Beneath the dust, ground-penetrating radar revealed something unexpected: the wreckage of a technological artifact, buried three meters deep and approximately four hundred meters long. Excavation revealed what appears to be an ancient space probe or vessel of unknown origin, constructed from materials that do not match any known manufacturing tradition, human or alien. The artifact is heavily damaged, consistent with a high-velocity impact, but enough structure survives to confirm deliberate construction. The dust has preserved it perfectly, a shroud over technology that may predate human civilization by millions of years.

Analysis of the artifact is ongoing, complicated by the dust contamination that makes clean-room conditions impossible to maintain at the excavation site. What has been determined is that the artifact was designed for interstellar travel, based on the presence of what appear to be radiation shielding and a propulsion system operating on principles not yet understood. Its trajectory, reconstructed from the impact angle and burial depth, suggests it originated from outside the local stellar neighborhood. Muslin-Shroud, a world so unremarkable it nearly escaped survey entirely, may hold the key to proving that interstellar civilizations existed long before humanity looked up at the stars.
